## Historical audit: S0022

**Scope.** This is chunk 1 of 2 only. All citations below refer to source **S0022**, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_2/results/r1/fixed_h/r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_92056365/trajectory.jsonl`. Neither the reference nor rendered images are visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The stated goal was a separately meshed indoor reconstruction matching a single photograph’s viewpoint, framing, placement and materials. The student’s inventory interprets it as a window-side cafeteria; that interpretation is not independent image verification (student response, line 3). |
| Student response and execution, lines 3–5 | The first program constructed multiple named assets: architecture, booths, tables, chairs, pendants and plants. It specified chair backs, seats, pedestals and bases; pendant shades, cords and ceiling roses; and palm stems and leaflets. These are emitted hierarchy and intended connections, not proof of physical contact or correct geometry. It used colored materials, a near-monochrome conversion, camera and three area lights; no image texture is specified. Step 1 reported `ok: true` and saved a render and blend file in 28.02 seconds. |
| Review and revision, lines 7–10 | The next student request included the first render and reference and asked for comparison. The student **reported**, rather than independently established here, that the foreground pendant and palm were out of frame, furniture too pale, shrubs too prominent, ceiling line too low and booth too small. The revised program moved the pendant and palm, enlarged/repositioned booths, darkened materials, raised the ceiling, moved shrubs back, added table accessories, changed the camera target and adjusted lighting. Chair rotations and palm frond directions specify poses, whose correctness is unverified. |
| Validation, lines 11–12 | Step 2 reported `ok: true`, saved another render and blend file in 36.03 seconds, and was selected. This is **technical execution success**, not formal proof of scene fidelity or of improvement over step 1. No failure, empty patch or technical interruption is visible in this chunk. Overall formal outcome remains unknown. |
| Input and exploration, lines 1–2, 7–9 | The visible guidance was the reconstruction and review procedure plus execution feedback; no teacher-authored detection, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is shown. The student independently generated and revised programs; the recorded CLI sessions show zero tool calls. This does not establish what may appear in the unseen chunk. |

**Transferable lesson:** A successful render and a named part hierarchy establish execution and emitted structure, not visual completeness, object connections or camera accuracy. Comparing a full render against an inventory can guide a revision, but the reported discrepancies remain the student’s observations.

**Task-specific uncertainty:** Whether the revisions actually brought the pendant and palm into frame, improved furniture appearance or fixed the ceiling line is unknown. Material/texture fidelity, object counts and overlaps, part contact, pose, camera alignment, lighting and any render artifacts cannot be independently assessed without the images. Hidden furniture and exterior geometry were also explicitly uncertain in the student’s inventory (lines 3 and 9).
